endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: entrainment of the circadian melatonin rhythm (proportion of patients entrained, based on melatonin/aMT6s measurements)

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was defined as the proportion of patients who were entrained (as defined based on melatonin measurements).

On 5/12/12 (in Version 9 of Study 3201 protocol), the Applicant changed the primary endpoint to entrainment of the circadian melatonin rhythm (from average nTST) which required fewer subject numbers to power the study (from 160 to 84) citing difficulty in subject recruitment; secondary endpoints included clinical outcomes, as measured by sleep, daytime naps and functionality.

Eighty-four patients (tasimelteon 42; placebo 42) were randomized to receive tasimelteon (20 mg/day) or placebo. Of these 84 patients who were randomized to study drug, 62 (73.8%) patients completed the Randomization Phase and 22 (26.2%) patients discontinued early.

result.text: Entrainment of the melatonin rhythm significantly greater with tasimelteon vs placebo (% difference = 17.4; p = 0.0171); clinical response (entrained + N24CRS >=3) % difference = 23.7; p = 0.0028

citations.quote: The proportion of Non-24 patients who were entrained after tasimelteon treatment during the Randomization Phase was statistically significantly greater than the proportion of Non-24 patients who were entrained after placebo treatment (% difference = 17.4; p = 0.0171).

The proportion of patients who were entrained (aMT6s) and had a clinical response rate (N24CRS) \ge 3 after tasimelteon treatment during the Randomization Phase was statistically significantly greater than the proportion of patients who were entrained and had a clinical response rate \ge 3 after placebo treatment (% difference = 23.7; p = 0.0028).
